sources.title: Meituan backend interview note linked-list-add prompt

claims.text: Two non-empty linked lists represent non-negative integers, digits are stored in reverse order, and the result must be returned as a linked list.
Under the explicit decimal-digit node representation, low-to-high streaming addition with one carry state handles unequal lengths and final carry without materializing the whole integer.
The exact implementation passes representative, zero, unequal-length, carry-chain and final-carry cases.

validation.reported_stdout: PASS examples=6 reverse-order=true unequal-length=true carry-chain=true final-carry=true zero=true

boundary_tests.expected: 0 -> 0 -> 0 -> 1 across unequal lengths and carry chain

findings: The repository source is recoverable and explicitly constrains non-empty linked lists, non-negative integers, reverse-order digit storage, and linked-list output.
The candidate removes the unrelated InnoDB/B+tree generated baseline and remains on the linked-list-add topic throughout.
The Java fence is a complete compilable class with its node type and addTwoNumbers implementation.
The loop invariant handles unequal lengths and preserves a final carry after both inputs are exhausted.
Fresh deterministic tests cover the representative example, zero, unequal lengths, carry chains, single-digit carry and final new high digit.
The one-decimal-digit ListNode schema is presented as an implementation contract rather than attributed to missing source detail.
No fabricated project experience or unsupported production claim is present.
